summary: Windows App Control (formerly WDAC) restricts which executables and scripts can run on a Windows host and used to break Ansible. Since Ansible 2.19 and ansible.windows 3.1.0, Ansible can run on hosts with App Control enabled, but the support is experimental and modules should be tested first.
questions: Does Ansible work on Windows hosts with WDAC enabled?
Which Ansible version added support for Windows App Control?
Is WDAC support in Ansible production ready?
Why did Ansible fail on hosts with Windows Defender Application Control?

answer_card.title: Ansible and Windows App Control (WDAC)
answer_card.answer_md:
Windows App Control (formerly Windows Defender Application Control, WDAC) restricts what executables and scripts can run. It used to make Ansible fail. Starting with **Ansible 2.19** and **`ansible.windows` 3.1.0**, Ansible can run on hosts with App Control enabled.

This is **experimental** and may change. Not every PowerShell module is guaranteed to work, and a module could allow code to run in ways App Control normally blocks, so test all modules with WDAC enabled before production use.
